results.title: Micro-Cap Industrial Stock Locked in 5% Upper Circuit on Monday After Company Announces FY26 Results; Net Profit Jumps to Rs 4.50 Crore - Dalal Street Investment Journal
results.content: # Micro-Cap Industrial Stock Locked in 5% Upper Circuit on Monday After Company Announces FY26 Results; Net Profit Jumps to Rs 4.50 Crore. Magnus Steel & Infra reported 6x growth in FY26 revenue to Rs 22.58 crore, while Q4 net profit surged over 590 per cent YoY; company also approved Rs 45 crore preferential issue for expansion plans. In this segment, **Magnus Steel and Infra** remained sharply in focus after the company announced strong FY26 financial performance along with a Rs 45 crore preferential fund raise. Following the development, Magnus Steel share price was locked in the 5 per cent **Upper Circuit** at Rs 151.40 on Monday. Magnus Steel and Infra reported revenue from operations of Rs 22.58 crore in FY26 as against Rs 3.19 crore in FY25, registering a sharp growth of 607.8 per cent YoY. Net profit stood at Rs 1.52 crore in Q4FY26 compared to Rs 0.22 crore reported in Q4FY25, registering a sharp jump of over 590 per cent YoY, indicating strong quarterly business momentum.

results.title: TIM negotiates new Vale contracts as corporate revenue jumps - BNamericas
results.content: TIMstarted 2026 by strengthening its presence in the corporate and industrial market and with plans to expand its activities with Vale, with new projects underway with the mining company, according to executives from the operator. During a press conference held this Wednesday (6), the company highlighted the progress of the B2B segment, whose contracted revenue grew 30% in the first quarter and exceeded 1 billion (bn) reais, driven by projects in mining, energy, digital infrastructure, and artificial intelligence (AI). In response to BNamericas, TIM’s B2B vice president, Fábio Costa, said that the company has been expanding its presence with Vale and is already negotiating new contracts with the company under a “master connectivity contract” announcedlast year. According to him, the project is considered “super important” for the operator, especially due to the growing demand for advanced connectivity and industrial digitalization solutions. When commenting on Vale’s previousrelationship with Vivo, Costa said that the mining company has different operational fronts and connectivity demands, but that TIM’s expectation is to become the main telecom provider.
